entries.lesson_title: Deriving Transfer Functions from Differential Equations
entries.core_move: Convert a circuit input-output differential equation into a Laplace-domain transfer function by applying zero-initial-condition derivative properties and isolating $H(s)=Y(s)/X(s) as the rational expression used for pole$, stability, and frequency-response analysis.

Derive first-order RC circuit transfer functions in the s-domain by replacing capacitors with 1/(sC), applying voltage or current division to form $H(s)=Y(s)/X(s)$, and interpreting the resulting pole-zero structure in terms of time constant and low-pass or high-pass behavior.

Derive the second-order input-output differential equation of an RLC circuit from Kirchhoff laws and element relations, identifying the coefficients that will become the circuit transfer function denominator and pole locations.

Derive the RLC circuit transfer function $H(s)=Y(s)/X(s) by Laplace-transforming its differential equation and expressing the result as a rational s-domain input-output ratio for pole and stability analysis$.

entries.lesson_title: Computing Poles of an RLC Circuit
entries.core_move: Compute the poles of an RLC circuit by solving the denominator of its transfer function as a characteristic polynomial in s and locating the roots used for stability interpretation.

Determine whether an RLC circuit transfer function is BIBO stable by checking that all computed poles lie strictly in the left half of the s-plane and interpreting any right-half-plane or imaginary-axis pole as a nondecaying circuit mode.

entries.lesson_title: Circuit Descriptions in Time, Frequency, and $s$ Domains
entries.core_move: Convert a circuit description among its time-domain differential equation, frequency-response form, and s-domain transfer function, interpreting poles and stability consistently across domains.
